implementation_notes: jsonwebtoken is the realization: a serde-serializable struct is the claim set, Header::new(Algorithm::RS256) plus Header.kid carries the profile, and encode(&header, &claims, &EncodingKey) returns the compact assertion, with EncodingKey::from_rsa_pem/from_ec_pem/from_ed_pem covering asymmetric keys. What replaces the classic structure: a struct plus two functions replace the builder classes - encode on the issuing side and decode(&token, &DecodingKey, &Validation) on the consuming side, where Validation pins the algorithm, the audience, the issuer and the required spec claims. The type system checks the shape of the claims, never their meaning, so exp, aud and jti still have to be fields of the struct and entries in Validation; josekit or the raw rsa/p256 crates cover the manual route if the dependency is unacceptable.
pitfalls: EncodingKey::from_rsa_pem parses the PEM each time it is called - the crate documents that the key should be built once and reused, which also avoids repeated key validation.
Algorithm and key construction are independent, so an HMAC secret paired with Algorithm::RS256 compiles and fails only at runtime; construct header and key together in one function.
On the consuming side Validation defaults must be checked explicitly: audience and issuer checks only run when those fields are set, so an unset aud accepts a token meant for someone else.
exp is seconds since the epoch; a millisecond timestamp or a literal zero mints an assertion that is already expired, and encode will not warn.
